newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West spot power slips as weather moderates.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West spot power slips as weather moderates.

text.p: Spot power prices in the western U.S. fell further as temperatures continued to rise, market sources said Friday.
"Temperatures are supposed to moderate more after Tuesday, but it still remains to be seen," said one Pacific Northwest trader.
He noted the Christmas holiday will likely put even more of a damper on electricity usage in the middle of next week.
A trader in Tucson, Ariz., also said recent freezing temperatures have eased, and regional loads were down.
"We are back on coal," he explained, noting that some utilities were forced to pay much higher combustion turbine prices for spot power during this week's cold snap.
Firm, peak electricity at the California-Oregon border (COB) on Monday was quoted $27.00-28.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), compared with $35.00-38.00 for Friday.
Firm, off-peak COB power for Monday was little changed near $20.00.
Monday firm, peak power at Mid-Columbia (Mid-C) was pegged at $26.00-$28.00, compared with $35.00-40.00 Wednesday.
Firm, peak Palo Verde (PV) electricity for Monday was quoted $25.00-26.00, compared with $40.00-45.00.
Off-peak PV for firm delivery Monday was quoted near $18.00.
Monday firm, peak prices at Four Corners were in line with PV at around $25.00. Firm, off-peak Four Corners power was assessed at $16.00-18.00.
